market_holds: Spot $1.00 at the 2026-11-20 close (sealed baseline, Yahoo bars), 62.7% below the 52-week high and 0.4% above the 52-week low; -14.2% over 5 sessions, including -9.0% on the 16 Nov day the results date was announced (stocktitan). There is no usable option chain (empty chain), so no implied move. 20-day realised vol is 92% annualised, giving a one-day band of about 5.8%. The stock is extremely thin: 20-day average volume is 14.3k shares (~$14k/day), and on 2026-11-20 it traded 1,780 shares with an intraday low of $0.86 (Yahoo chart). The last four prints, close to close on the release day: Q3'25 (9 Dec 2025) -4.2%, then -2.8%, -3.6% and -5.5% over the next three days; Q4'25 (14 Apr 2026) -4.2%; Q1'26 (9 Jun 2026) +0.3%; Q2'26 (18 Aug 2026) -18.8%, then -8.0% and -11.8% the next two days. Consensus is effectively absent: Digrin's Q3 estimates are blank, Seeking Alpha's are paywalled, and the one cited Q2 revenue forecast was RMB375.9m against RMB273.4m actual, which shows how stale the street number is. Management gives no guidance. The Q2 call stepped up marketing from September and offered no breakeven date. Liquidity is backstopped by the parent: THRI convertible-note tranches of US$15.8m (July), US$15m (10 Sep) and US$15m (16 Oct 2026, SEC 6-Ks), with one more expected in Q1 2027. The shareholders' deficit was RMB1.41bn at 30 June.
view: Q3 2026 is set up to look bad on the headline. In Q3 2025 the food-delivery subsidy war inflated the base: Tims system sales were +12.8% and system SSS +1.3%. The industry's own read for this quarter is worse than Q2. Luckin's self-operated SSS went from -5.3% in Q2 to -11.1% in Q3 2026 against the same subsidy base (Luckin 6-K, 3 Nov 2026). Tims' Q2 already showed SSS -17.8%, revenue -21.7% and a widening loss, and it added marketing from September. So Q3 revenue is likely around RMB270-290m (-20% to -25% against RMB358.0m), with losses no better and probably worse. That is a print a stale consensus will read as another miss. Against that, the stock has already fallen 63% from its high, sits at the $1 line, and fell 14% into the event on almost no volume. Every holder knows the business is shrinking, and the parent keeps funding it. The upside case is the new CEO's 'green shoots': loyalty members up about 40% and a possible sequential improvement in transactions after the September marketing push, framed as a turnaround. In a stock this thin, a single trade at 13:00 ET Monday can sit 10% either side of anything fundamental. The base rate of three negative prints in four, plus negative post-print drift, tilts me down. But nothing I can show says the decline is not already held in a $1 price after a 14% week, and the scored price will be set by a handful of trades.
unpriced: Possibly the size of the headline revenue miss against a stale, sparsely maintained consensus (Q2 missed it by 27%) on a print that laps a subsidy-inflated base. I cannot show that the price does not hold it: the stock has already fallen to its low into the date, and with ~$14k a day of turnover there is no informed marginal holder whose expectation I can read.

recommendation.reason: Comps (Q3'25 system sales +12.8% on delivery subsidies), the industry read-across (Luckin SSS fell from -5.3% to -11.1% in Q3) and the stock's record (3 of 4 prints down, -18.8% on Q2) all lean down. But the stock has already fallen 14% in five days to its 52-week low at $1, turns over about $14k a day, and has no consensus I can verify. So I cannot show what the price does not hold, and the scored 13:00 ET print may be a single odd-lot trade. My lean is below the 65 bar.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A sequential improvement in SSS or transactions in Q3 (better than Q2's -17.8%) plus a credible breakeven timeline or a parent take-private or recapitalisation announcement would turn a thin $1 stock sharply up.

self_critique: The strongest case against a down lean: the stock has already lost 63% and fell 14% into the date, a shrinking-revenue print is what every holder expects, and a new CEO with fresh marketing and parent funding can easily frame Q3 as the trough. Any sequential stabilisation in a $1 stock with a tiny float can produce a +10-20% print. The case against acting at all: the scored 13:00 ET price can be set by a few hundred shares.
approach_notes: Rebuilding the comp from the counterparty (Luckin's Q3 SSS) and the prior-year release paid off. The playbook's 'priced in is a claim to prove' cuts both ways here: with no consensus and $14k/day of turnover, I could not prove the price held the decline or that it did not, and the playbook gives no guidance for names this illiquid.
